messages:
maria.l: quick sanity check — noticed a weird behaviour when chart has both `env:` entries and `envFrom:` pointing at an ExternalSecret mounted in a different namespace. app fails to start with duplicate env var error on k8s 1.26. anyone seen this?

ben: hm, do you mean duplicate keys in the container env list, or a secret collision because namespace diff?

maria.l: duplicate keys in the generated pod spec. helm template output shows the same env var twice — once from our explicit `env:` and once from the `envFrom` projection. here's the relevant values snippet: 

```yaml
# values.yaml (app):
app:
  env:
    - name: REDIS_URL
      value: redis://redis.svc:6379
  extraEnvFrom:
    - externalSecret: 
        name: app-secrets
        namespace: infra-secrets
        prefix: ""
```

and the template: 
```tpl
env: {{ toYaml .Values.app.env | indent 8 }}
{{- if .Values.app.extraEnvFrom }}
envFrom:{{- range .Values.app.extraEnvFrom }}
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .externalSecret.name }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
```

sai: that template looks fine at glance. Helm just renders what you tell it. Are you using `toYaml` for envFrom too by accident somewhere else?

maria.l: I thought so too. But the generated pod actually has two entries: one env REDIS_URL and another env REDIS_URL from the secret key ref (external-secret was syncing a key called REDIS_URL). k8s then complains about duplicate env variable names.

tim: oh — ExternalSecret sync producing the same key name is expected if secret contains that key. Helm envFrom just injects the whole secret, so yes duplication happens. Two ways to handle: 1) remove the explicit `env` entry and rely on secret, or 2) keep explicit and use `envFrom` but add `optional: true`/prefix so keys don't collide, or 3) explicitly map secret keys to env var names with `env:` and avoid envFrom.

ben: also consider namespace. envFrom with secretRef will reference the secret in the same namespace as the pod. Since your ExternalSecret creates secret in `infra-secrets` namespace, are you doing a cross-namespace secretRef? k8s secretRef for envFrom must be in same ns as pod. If you attempted cross-ns, maybe you have a sync that copies secret into app namespace and that's where collision arises.

maria.l: yes the operator copies into `apps-prod` namespace via a `SecretStore` + ExternalSecret mapping. so there is a plain secret in the pod ns containing `REDIS_URL`.

sai: quick patch suggestion: guard the envFrom in the chart with a function that removes keys that are explicitly defined. e.g. render env mapping as explicit entries, then only add envFrom if `skipEnvFromOnCollision: false`?

maria.l: thought about that. was thinking of a values-driven checkbox like `preventEnvCollision: true`. But would rather not ship a complex tpl. any small helm helper snippets?

ben: we sometimes use a helper to compute set of explicit env names and only render envFrom if `envFromPrefix` set. Example helper: 
```tpl
{{- define "app.envFromAllowed" -}}
{{- if .Values.app.envFromPrefix }}true{{- else }}false{{- end -}}
{{- end -}}
```
Then docs tell teams to set prefix so keys don't collide.

tim: another pattern: translate `envFrom` into explicit `env` entries in the template by iterating secret keys at render time — but helm can't inspect remote secret contents. So that's not viable.

maria.l: right, not available at template time. so prefix seems simplest. but several services assume `REDIS_URL` key exists in secret no prefix. making team change all secrets is annoying.

sai: fallback — keep explicit env entries for important keys and keep envFrom for misc ones. That avoids duplicates for the few keys we care about. e.g. explicit `REDIS_URL` in env, envFrom for the rest. That is what you already have, but collision still happens because the secret contains REDIS_URL. But k8s will still report duplicate names at pod creation. So if you keep explicit, you need to avoid envFrom injecting the same name. Which brings us back to prefix or removing key from secret.

ben: short-term workaround: add `envFrom` only in non-prod overlays where secrets don't include those keys, and in prod overlay set `extraEnvFrom: []` and rely on the secret. Or add a `skipEnvFromInProd: true` value and change prod values.

maria.l: I can do an overlay change for our prod kustomize/helm values to remove `envFrom`. I'll open a tiny PR to set `extraEnvFrom: []` in `values-prod.yaml` and leave chart default as-is.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: maria-l/patch/remove-envfrom-prod #3421 — staging will run after merge :rocket:

maria.l: thanks. one more question: is there any reason to ever prefer explicit `env` over mapping secret keys to env with `valueFrom.secretKeyRef`? i.e. `- name: REDIS_URL
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: app-secrets
      key: REDIS_URL` vs envFrom?

tim: explicit mapping is safer if you want control and avoid collisions. envFrom is convenient when you trust the secret shape. For multi-tenant charts, explicit mapping + documented optional keys is the most robust.

ben: agreed. explicit mapping is the only way to avoid these collisions without changing secret contents or prefixes. It's a bit more verbose, but you can provide a values helper to auto-generate mapping from a `secretKeys:` map in values.

maria.l: ok will do the prod overlay change first and then propose a follow-up to add `secretKeys` map to chart so teams can prefer explicit mapping. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

sai: +1, lmk if you want help with the values generator helper.

maria.l: will tag you on the PR. end.
